title: Conformal Risk Control
research_question: Can conformal prediction be generalized from miscoverage control to finite-sample control of the expected value of a broad class of bounded monotone losses?
methodology: The paper defines conformal risk control for a family of set-valued or otherwise nested predictors whose losses are bounded and non-increasing as a tuning parameter increases. It derives a finite-sample calibration rule and proves expected-risk guarantees under exchangeability, then studies lower bounds, distribution-shift extensions, multiple-risk variants, and failure modes for non-monotone losses. The method is evaluated over repeated random calibration/test splits on tumor segmentation, multilabel classification, hierarchical ImageNet classification, and Natural Questions retrieval and reading.

key_findings.finding: For exchangeable examples and bounded, right-continuous, non-increasing loss functions, the proposed calibration rule controls the expected test loss at the target level in finite samples.
Ordinary split conformal prediction is recovered as a special case when the loss is the indicator of prediction-set miscoverage.

Under additional regularity assumptions, the attainable expected risk is within order 1/n of the requested risk level, although the authors note that the constant in their lower bound may not be tight.
Across the four empirical application domains, average held-out risk was close to the requested risk level over repeated calibration/test splits.
The basic conformal-risk-control rule does not provide a general finite-sample guarantee for arbitrary non-monotone losses; the paper gives examples where it can fail badly.

The framework provides extensions for certain distribution shifts, including density-ratio weighting and bounds whose degradation depends on total-variation differences between calibration and test distributions.

limitations: The central finite-sample result relies on exchangeability in its base setting.
The principal theorem requires losses to be bounded, non-increasing, and right-continuous in the calibration parameter.
General finite-sample control is not established for arbitrary non-monotone losses.
Distribution-shift extensions require additional assumptions such as known or suitably handled density ratios; estimating covariate-shift weights is not solved by the core method.
The guarantee is primarily marginal expected-risk control rather than an instance-wise conditional guarantee.
The framework controls a supplied loss but does not itself define evidence completeness, longitudinal state transitions, or omission of superseded work items.
raw_claims: Conformal risk control extends conformal calibration from binary miscoverage to more general bounded losses.
The finite-sample guarantee applies to exchangeable calibration and test examples.
The loss must become no worse as the predictor is made more conservative through the calibration parameter.
Classical conformal prediction fits the framework by using a miscoverage indicator as the loss.
The expected risk can approach the desired level at an order-1/n rate under additional assumptions.
Non-monotone losses can invalidate the basic finite-sample guarantee.
The experiments include segmentation, multilabel classification, hierarchical classification, and question answering.
Repeated-split experiments show held-out risks close to their specified targets.
Distribution-shift variants can use importance weighting when the relevant density ratio is available.
Total-variation distance can be used to quantify deterioration of the risk bound under arbitrary marginal shifts.
